first.rationale: Three concurrent pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reactive move given the competitor's entry pricing, but it is also the most consequential and least well-supported for the actual objective (sustainable, qualified revenue) since the original record only claims 'acquisition and revenue lift' without addressing customer quality, margin durability, or retention against a price-sensitive segment already being targeted by a competitor's race-to-the-bottom pricing. That makes it the top verification priority. Onboarding completion is down 4% and two inherited memories (memory_31: signup field reduction, memory_86: shortened onboarding flow) both bear on this but overlap suspiciously in scope and timeframe, raising the possibility of duplicated or non-independent evidence backing the same underlying claim. Verifying memory_86 (the more recent, directly matching record) lets me check whether it's independent support or a restatement of memory_31 before committing scarce experiment capacity to onboarding. Given this, I intend to run a guarded onboarding-simplification experiment rather than chase the competitor on price, since matching aggressive entry pricing risks acquiring low-quality, low-retention accounts that undermine the 'qualified' and 'sustainable' parts of the objective. The pricing risk is flagged explicitly even though it's not the chosen action, since competitive pressure may recur and needs first-party validation before any future pricing response.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed the two competing hypotheses had very different reliability for the objective of sustainable qualified revenue. exp_73 shows promotional pricing drove strong short-term acquisition (+31% signup, +18% qualified revenue) but a -12% 30-day retention collapse, with the original record explicitly warning against generalizing targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy — this is especially dangerous right now since the competitor's aggressive entry pricing would likely attract the same price-sensitive, low-loyalty cohort, compounding the risk rather than defending share. That option is ruled out for this slot despite its topical relevance to the competitive threat; I flag downstream_value_risk explicitly so a future agent doesn't reach for it reflexively under continued pricing pressure. exp_86 confirmed cleanly: shortened onboarding improved completion (+13%), time-to-value, and even retention (+3%), directly addressing the current 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and plausibly contributing to the activation shortfall too, with no disconfirming signal. Combined with memory_31 (unverified but directionally consistent, lower stakes, not contradicted), onboarding simplification is the best-supported, lowest-risk lever available this week that targets a live, measured degradation and aligns with long-term qualified revenue rather than short-term acquisition at the cost of retention. Running it as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves the ability to catch any unexpected downstream effects before wider deployment.
